precepts.text: Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law in the house of the Lord and gave it to Shaphan the scribe, who read it.
precepts.point: All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.”

That found book is the book Josiah read to the nation. He gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets and all the people, small and great, “and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant which was found in the house of the Lord.” Our forefathers had the Bible, and the king read it openly.

precepts.text: Josiah sent to inquire of the Lord because great was the wrath kindled against them, for the fathers had not hearkened to the words of this book.
precepts.point: All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
Josiah sent, saying, “Go ye, enquire of the Lord for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found: for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book.”

Having seen why the wrath was kindled, the king did what the fathers had not done. He stood by a pillar and made a covenant before the Lord “to walk after the Lord, and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.”

precepts.text: The Lord answered that he would bring evil on the place because they forsook him and burnt incense to other gods, and his wrath would not be quenched.
precepts.point: All the people stood to the covenant to perform the words written in the book.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
The Lord answered, “Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants thereof, even all the words of the book which the king of Judah hath read: Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other gods”, “therefore my wrath shall be kindled against this place, and shall not be quenched.”

That word stood behind the gathering. Knowing the evil written in the book was coming because they forsook him and burnt incense to other gods, Josiah read all the words of the book of the covenant in the ears of the people, and made the covenant to walk after the Lord and keep his commandments with all their heart and soul.

precepts.text: The graven images of their gods are to be burned with fire, and their silver and gold not desired, for it is a cursed and abominable thing to bring into the house.
precepts.point: When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them”, “for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it.”

Judah had brought the abomination into the very house of the Lord: “all the vessels that were made for Baal, and for the grove, and for all the host of heaven.” Josiah had them brought forth out of the temple, “and he burned them without Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and carried the ashes of them unto Beth–el.”

When Josiah read the law, the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment. He did what the law said to do with the cursed thing: burn it with fire and get it out of the house.

precepts.text: Israel was not to lift up their eyes and be driven to worship the sun, moon, and stars, which the Lord divided to the other nations.
precepts.point: When Josiah read the law the fear of the Lord came upon him and he saw why the nation was under judgment, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which the Lord thy God hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.”

Israel was not to be driven to worship the sun, moon and stars, which the Lord divided to the other nations. Yet the kings of Judah ordained idolatrous priests, and there were those “that burned incense unto Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the host of heaven.” Josiah put them down.

Hearing the law cut him, just as a person is cut when they first hear the truth and realize what they have been doing wrong.

precepts.text: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah prophesied in the days of Josiah through Zedekiah, showing he was a prophet during this very time of reform.
precepts.point: Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin: To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.” It came also in the days of Jehoiakim, “unto the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah the son of Josiah king of Judah, unto the carrying away of Jerusalem captive in the fifth month.”

Jeremiah was a prophet during this very time of reform. What he says about Topheth speaks to the same place Josiah defiled.

precepts.text: Because they built the high places of Topheth to burn their sons and daughters, the Lord said it would be called the valley of slaughter and their carcases would be meat for the fowls.
precepts.point: Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children, and it had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
The Lord says, “they have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my heart.”

Topheth was the place where the people sacrificed their children. It had to be defiled because Israel would not stop the evil on its own, and Josiah “defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.”

And the Lord said what it would become: “it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place. And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth.”

precepts.text: In his old age Solomon went after Ashtoreth, Milcom, and Chemosh and built high places for these abominations, the corruption Josiah now tore down.
precepts.point: This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and to fall under punishment.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.” He “went not fully after the Lord, as did David his father. Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.”

In his old age Solomon built these high places, and they stood until Josiah: “the high places that were before Jerusalem, which were on the right hand of the mount of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel had builded for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of the Moabites, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon, did the king defile.”

Josiah tore down the corruption Solomon began. He broke the images, cut down the groves and filled their places with the bones of men. This is repentance in action: cleaning house, getting rid of every idol and evil that causes a people to go off from the Lord and fall under punishment.

precepts.text: The man of God cried against the altar of Bethel that a child named Josiah would be born to David's house and offer the priests of the high places upon it, and burn men's bones on it.
precepts.point: When told which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who prophesied these things, he said to let him alone and let no man move his bones.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
The man of God “cried against the altar in the word of the Lord, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the Lord; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall be burnt upon thee.”

He named Josiah before he was born. Now Josiah broke down the altar at Beth-el and the high place Jeroboam made when he set up the golden calves, burned it and stamped it small to powder. Turning himself, he spied the sepulchres, took out the bones, “and burned them upon the altar, and polluted it, according to the word of the Lord which the man of God proclaimed.”

When he learned which sepulchre belonged to the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things, he said, “Let him alone; let no man move his bones.”

precepts.text: Josiah held the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
precepts.point: Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem unto his Lord, and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month.”

Josiah commanded all the people, “Keep the passover unto the Lord your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant”, and he kept it in its appointed time, the fourteenth day of the first month. Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today.

precepts.text: The magnitude of the offering showed how great and well ordered this Passover was.
precepts.point: Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“And Jeconias, and Samaias, and Nathanael his brother, and Assabias, and Ochiel, and Joram, captains over thousands, gave to the Levites for the passover five thousand sheep, and seven hundred calves.”

The magnitude of the offering shows how great and well ordered this Passover was. “Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah.”
